correctness.rationale: Exact independent incidence-cell multinomial law. Rare triple cells have probability O(n^-1/2); singleton counts have jointly independent n^(1/4)-Gaussian fluctuations, pair counts independent Poisson limits, and these blocks become independent via their joint moment generating function. Connectivity reduces to pair categories with high probability and total ordinary count differs from selected singletons by a tight bridge count. The total variation rate follows from multivariate rare-cell Poisson approximation. All 96 deterministic finite checks passed; finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The natural critical transmission scaling makes hub-to-hub connectivity nontrivial even with only finitely many hubs. The result gives the complete joint law of an epidemic/transport cluster: discrete random hub topology determines the O(sqrt n) physical outbreak size and selects the n^(1/4) Gaussian fluctuation variance. This distinguishes rare bridge formation from ordinary population fluctuations and yields explicit nondegenerate multi-peaked outbreak laws, not an arbitrary finite slice.
